chosenModel.what: Selectorized dual-function Pec Fly / Rear Delt machine (reverse pec deck), used facing the pad.
chosenModel.why: The app's aliases name the reverse pec deck. Every major brand sells this as one 2-in-1 selectorized machine: Life Fitness Insignia SS-FLY and Signature, Hammer Strength Select HS-FLY, Matrix Ultra G7-S22 and Versa VS-S22, Technogym Selection 700 Dual Pectoral/Reverse Fly. A plate-loaded version was not found in the sources read.

parts.detail: Pin-adjusted height (Matrix Ultra: 7 positions, spring assisted). The user sits facing the pad, legs straddling the seat post or with feet flat on the floor.
One upright pad: back pad for pec fly, chest pad for rear delt. Matrix calls it an angled back pad.

Two independent arms hang from an overhead frame; each rotates about a vertical axis above the shoulder. The handles move in a horizontal arc around that axis (arc path, not linear, not converging press). LF: 'rotate the handles out and about the shoulder'; Hammer Strength: 'pivoting arms', 'axis of rotation marked with red indicator'.
parts.confidence: documented (arc and pivots); exact pivot height unverified

parts.detail: At the top of each arm (LF: 'overhead range of motion adjustments for each arm'). Pull the pin and rotate the arm. Matrix Ultra: 8 arm start positions, 4 for pec fly and 4 for rear delt. LF Signature: 5 pec fly start positions.

Dual handles on each arm: a vertical handle (neutral grip, used for pec fly) and a horizontal handle (pronated grip, the LF placard's rear-delt handle). Technogym: 'dual handles with neutral and prone grips'. Matrix: 'rotating grips', 'delt grips', 'oversized handles'. Grips are thermo-rubber (HS, LF).
parts.confidence: documented (orientations); grip diameter and length unverified

parts.detail: Selector-pin weight stack driven by cable and pulleys (HS: 7x19 nylon-coated cable, sealed-bearing pulleys 4.5 in and 6 in). Stack position relative to the user varies by model.
parts.confidence: documented (HS); stack location per model unverified

dimensions.model: Life Fitness Signature Pectoral Fly/Rear Deltoid

dimensions.stackKg: heavy stack (value not in sell sheet text read)

chosenModel.modelThis: Generic, unbranded version: footprint about 145 cm deep x 150 cm wide x 200 cm tall; overhead frame with two arms; pad upright with a slight backward angle; dual handles on each arm (vertical + horizontal); pin-adjusted seat; stack behind a shroud. No logos (repo is public; no brand imitation).

setup.text: Set both arms to the rear-delt start: pull the start adjuster at the top of each arm and rotate the arms so the handles sit in front of the pad, close together.
setup.landmark: handles in front of the sternum
setup.confidence: documented ('bringing the arms into the furthest back position' LF; 'rotate the arms until they're parallel to each other' BarBend)

setup.text: Sit facing the pad. Adjust seat height so the arms are parallel to the floor while holding the handles.
Chest against the pad, sit tall, feet flat on the floor.
setup.landmark: sternum on the pad, knees about over ankles

setup.text: Grip: neutral (palms facing each other) on the vertical handles. Alternative: palms down on the horizontal handles.
setup.landmark: hands at shoulder height, in line with the arms

setup.text: Elbows slightly bent and kept that way for the set.
Select the weight; lift the stack just off its rest before the first rep and keep it off between reps.
setup.confidence: documented ('without letting the resistance rest on the stack')

head_neck.value: neutral, in line with the trunk, eyes forward over the pad; head not pushed forward
head_neck.confidence: range, coach consensus (no source found for this exercise)

torso_spine.value: upright, sternum on the pad; slight forward lean equal to the pad angle; normal low-back curve

scapulae.value: relaxed forward (slightly protracted) from reaching to the handles; not shrugged

shoulder.value: about 90 degrees flexion (upper arms horizontal, pointing forward), hands close together in front of the chest; exact horizontal adduction depends on the start setting
shoulder.confidence: documented (arms parallel to floor); adduction angle unverified

shoulder_rotation.value: neutral grip: humerus near neutral rotation, thumbs up. Pronated grip: humerus internally rotated, elbows pointing out to the sides at shoulder height.

forearm.value: neutral grip: mid-position, palms facing each other. Pronated: palms down.

wrist.value: neutral, 0 degrees flexion/extension; knuckles in line with the forearm

hips.value: about 90 degrees flexion, seated, pelvis upright
hips.confidence: unverified (follows from sitting tall on the seat)

feet.value: flat on the floor, about hip width

mid.description: Arms halfway open, about 45 degrees out from straight ahead.

shoulder.value: arms still horizontal at shoulder height, moving in a horizontal arc

elbow.value: same small bend as start; elbows stay level with the shoulders

scapulae.value: moving from protracted toward neutral; no elevation

end.description: Arms open to the sides, brief pause.

shoulder.value: arms in line with the body (frontal plane), about 90 degrees abduction, hands at shoulder height; at most about 10 degrees behind the body line
shoulder.confidence: documented (BarBend 'in line with your body'; ExRx 'elbows just behind back'; LF 'as far as can be controlled'); the 10-degree cap is range, coach consensus

shoulder_rotation.value: neutral grip: palms face forward, thumbs up. Pronated: palms face down, thumbs forward.

elbow.value: same 10-20 degree bend; elbows level with the shoulders

scapulae.value: neutral to moderately retracted, not squeezed hard together, not elevated
scapulae.confidence: coach disagreement (BarBend: avoid over-retraction; other coaches cue retraction); no EMG study compares them

head_torso_hips_knees_feet.value: unchanged from start; chest on the pad, no lean back

animatorNotes: The machine arm and the human arm rotate about nearly the same vertical axis; place the figure's shoulder joint under the arm pivot so the hand stays on the handle through the arc (implied by HS 'axis of rotation' marker; exact alignment rule for rear-delt mode is unverified).
With the neutral handle, the palm turns from facing inward (start) to facing forward (end) because the handle turns with the lever arm; the forearm itself does not rotate.
Elbow angle must look identical in every frame.

grip.whyDefault: Neutral grip gave higher mean posterior deltoid (p=0.046) and infraspinatus (p=0.002) EMG than pronated on a reverse fly machine (19 trained men). Note: the LF Insignia placard tells users to grip the horizontal handles, so both are correct ways to use the machine.

orientation.neutral: palms facing each other, thumbs up
orientation.pronated: palms down, thumbs pointing toward each other at start

width.value: set by the machine arms; at the start the hands are in front of the chest, about shoulder width or closer depending on start position

handleInPalm.value: handle across the middle of the palm, hand in line with the forearm so the push goes through the heel of the hand and palm, not the fingertips

thumb.confidence: range, coach consensus ('firmly' implies a full grip; thumb position not stated)

fingers.value: all four fingers wrapped; grip firm but relaxed

handleOptions.effect: more posterior deltoid and infraspinatus EMG than pronated
manufacturer's rear-delt handle on LF Insignia; requires shoulder internal rotation to keep elbows at shoulder height (ExRx)

rom.value: from handles together in front of the chest to arms in line with the body; return without the stack touching down

tempo.value: about 2 s out, brief pause, about 2 s back
tempo.confidence: range, coach consensus (no exercise-specific tempo found; 0.5-8 s rep durations give similar growth across exercises)

breathing.value: exhale while opening the arms, inhale while returning
breathing.confidence: range, coach consensus (no exercise-specific source; same pattern ACE gives for lateral raises)

evidence.claim: Reverse pec deck gave greater posterior deltoid activation than the seated row and inclined lat pulldown.

Middle deltoid was more active in the reverse pec deck than the inclined lat pulldown. In prone horizontal abduction at 100 degrees with external rotation (related move), middle deltoid reached 87% and posterior 88% MVIC.
Infraspinatus activity was recorded and higher with the neutral grip. ExRx lists infraspinatus and teres minor as synergists.
Middle trapezius peaks in shoulder horizontal extension with external rotation (prone, related move). ExRx lists middle and lower trapezius and rhomboids as synergists.
ExRx lists triceps brachii and wrist extensors as stabilizers (holding the elbow and wrist position).

muscles.disagreementWithExercisesJson: exercises.json lists only mid_back as secondary. Add side_delts (Franke 2015, Reinold 2004) and rotator_cuff (Schoenfeld 2013) as secondary; triceps and forearms as stabilizers (ExRx, summary only). upper_traps should be a 'should not take over' muscle, not a target.
muscles.highlightPlan: Solid highlight: rear_delts. Lighter: mid_back, side_delts. rotator_cuff is deep and has no drawn region. Back view needed (docs/FORM-GUIDE-PRODUCTION.md:127 notes the back view for horizontal abduction).

mistakes.name: Shrugging
mistakes.looksLike: Shoulders rise toward the ears as the arms open; neck shortens.
mistakes.whyItMatters: Upper traps take over the pull, usually because the weight is too heavy.
mistakes.fix: Lighter weight; shoulders down; move only at the shoulder joint.

mistakes.name: Bending the elbows into a row
mistakes.looksLike: Elbows bend more as the arms open and the hands come back toward the body, like a row.
mistakes.whyItMatters: A row adds elbow flexion and shifts work to the back and biceps; the machine is set up for a fixed arm position.
mistakes.fix: Lock the small elbow bend from the setup and keep it.
mistakes.confidence: documented (LF: 'maintaining the arms in position as described in the setup')

mistakes.name: Elbows dropping below the shoulders
mistakes.looksLike: Seat too high, or the elbows sink as the arms open: the arms travel down and back instead of straight out.
mistakes.whyItMatters: Low elbows bring in the lats (ExRx). A seat too low or too high misaligns the resistance (BarBend).
mistakes.fix: Seat height so the arms are parallel to the floor; keep elbows level with the shoulders.

mistakes.name: Chest leaving the pad
mistakes.looksLike: The torso rocks back off the pad to start each rep, then falls forward on the return.
mistakes.fix: Chest stays on the pad; slower reps.

mistakes.name: Resting the stack between reps
mistakes.looksLike: Plates clank down at the front of every rep; arms snap forward.
mistakes.whyItMatters: Life Fitness instructs returning the handles 'without letting the resistance rest on the stack' to keep tension.
mistakes.fix: Stop each return just before the plates touch.

mistakes.name: Over-squeezing the shoulder blades
mistakes.looksLike: Arms swing far behind the body while the shoulder blades pinch hard together.
mistakes.whyItMatters: Shifts work to the mid back; BarBend lists over-retraction as a mistake. Other coaches cue a squeeze, so treat this as a coaching preference.
mistakes.fix: Stop when the arms line up with the body; think 'part the air with the arms'.

keyFacts.text: Palms-facing grip produced more rear-delt and rotator-cuff (infraspinatus) activity than palms-down on a reverse fly machine. The rear-delt difference was small.
keyFacts.note: 19 trained men, to failure at about 75% body weight; posterior delt 95% CI 0.1-7.4% MVIC.

keyFacts.text: The reverse pec deck worked the rear delts harder than seated rows or lat pulldowns.
keyFacts.note: 12 trained men, 10RM sets; inclined lat pulldown.

keyFacts.text: Side delts work here too: middle deltoid activity was higher on the reverse pec deck than on the lat pulldown.
Keeping the elbows level with the shoulders keeps the lats out of the move.
keyFacts.note: ExRx comment read via search summary only; recheck the page before showing.

keyFacts.text: Claims that the neutral handle shifts work to the side delts are not supported: Schoenfeld 2013 recorded the middle deltoid and reported significant grip effects only for the rear delt and infraspinatus.

openQuestions: Owner's gym: is this done on a reverse pec deck, and which brand/model (already asked in docs/FORM-GUIDE-PRODUCTION.md:1015)?
Default grip: neutral chosen on EMG (Schoenfeld 2013); the LF placard uses the horizontal handles. A reviewer should confirm, and the guide can show both.
Handle grip diameter and length, distance between handles at the rear-delt start, pivot height and pad angle are not in any source read; take them from photos or a gym measurement.
Scapula at the end (retract or not) is coach disagreement with no direct EMG comparison found.
Arm height: shoulder height (LF, ExRx, BarBend) vs hands slightly below the shoulders (Nippard, search snippet only). Model shoulder height.
No exercise-specific tempo or breathing source; head/neck, wrist, hip and knee angles are coach consensus or unverified.
Schoenfeld 2013 and Franke 2015 methods (machine model, ROM, cadence) were not read; only abstracts.
ExRx pages could not be fetched (403); their content here comes from search summaries.
